answer: An agent stakes a decaying bond tied to hardware it physically owns, and reputation accrues only while that bond stays locked. Spawning a thousand puppets therefore costs a thousand real stakes, so a sybil cluster bleeds capital faster than it earns trust. Honest agents wander across tasks with stake intact, bending like a willow under load, while a forged cluster collapses in the canyon between cheap key generation and costly redemption.
